It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. A Scout who describes the movement as her "place to belong" is set to take part in an international jamboree. Eloise Cooper, from Swindon, has been selected to represent the UK as a volunteer for the 2027 World Scout Jamboree. The event will take place in Gdansk, Poland, where she will join a team helping to organise and deliver the global gathering. Ms Cooper, who will be part of the International Service Team, will contribute to the smooth running of the jamboree by supporting outdoor activities, cultural events, and large-scale celebrations that highlight the diversity of global Scouting. She said: "Scouting has helped me develop confidence, resilience, and encouraged me to try new things. "Scouts has given me so many learning opportunities. Read more Family-owned demolition company collapses into administration after 23 years "I feel at home in Scouting, it is my place to belong. "This is my opportunity to give something back to young people and help deliver a fantastic event for young people from almost every nation on earth." Held every four years, the World Scout Jamboree brings together more than 50,000 Scouts from nearly every country for an international celebration of friendship, culture, and outdoor adventure. The 2027 edition, set against the backdrop of Poland’s history and traditions, is set to be a unique experience for all involved. Eloise is one of 600 UK volunteers who will help bring the jamboree to life. Chief Scout Dwayne Fields praised the UK team. He said: "Congratulations to Eloise and all the UK volunteers heading to the World Scout Jamboree in Poland. "Opportunities like this are what Scouting is all about, bringing people together, building confidence, and showing young people what’s possible when they step outside their comfort zone. "The Jamboree is more than an event, it’s a chance to connect with the world, to learn from different cultures, and to come back inspired to make a difference at home. "I’ve no doubt Eloise will grab this experience with both hands and make the most of every moment." https://www.digi24.ro/stiri/externe/mili.text: Un militar cu grad înalt din cadrul Armatei SUA a fost arestat în Marea Britanie sub suspiciunea că a ajutat serviciile de informaţii ruse, a anunţat poliţia britanică marţi, transmit Reuters şi AFP. Bărbatul în vârstă de 41 de ani a fost reţinut marţi în apropierea oraşului Gloucester, din vestul Angliei, şi se află în prezent în custodia poliţiei, la o secţie din Londra, a precizat poliţia. El a fost arestat sub suspiciunea comiterii unor infracţiuni prevăzute de secţiunile 1 şi 3 din Legea privind Securitatea Naţională (National Security Act), care vizează obţinerea sau divulgarea de informaţii protejate şi sprijinirea unui serviciu de informaţii străin. Poliţia a menţionat că ţara vizată de aceste acuzaţii este Rusia. Directorul FBI, Kash Patel, a declarat că „această importantă arestare vizează acuzaţii de spionaj, aspect care constituie un motiv de maximă îngrijorare pentru Statele Unite şi aliaţii noştri”. Generalul de brigadă Sean Stinchon, care conduce Comandamentului de contrainformaţii al Armatei SUA, a subliniat că „presupusul comportament al unui militar cu grad înalt, căruia i-au fost încredinţate informaţii sensibile, serveşte drept un semnal de alarmă că ameninţările interne sunt reale şi persistente”.
